checks.invariant: A prune that fails or is interrupted leaves the database and archive consistent: the archive is unlinked only when the DB transaction did not commit.
checks.result: Failed. retention.prune (retention.py:126-131) unlinks the archive in the outer `except BaseException` without checking whether COMMIT went through. h.py check1 used a Connection subclass that raises SIGINT right after a successful COMMIT returns. Result: prune raised OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active') chained from KeyboardInterrupt. The archive was deleted. The DB had committed: audit rows 1-5 deleted, an audit_anchor row (last_id 5, archive c1.jsonl.gz, sha256 3628...) and audit_pruned row #8 present. verify() returned ok with pruned_through 5. verify_archives([archive]) raised FileNotFoundError and verify_archives([]) failed with an anchor/archive count mismatch. cmd_prune (cli.py:321-323) catches only ValueError/FileExistsError/RuntimeError, so the operator sees a traceback, and a re-run finds nothing to prune.

checks.invariant: Timing prerequisite: a real asynchronous SIGINT that arrives while a real sqlite3 COMMIT runs surfaces inside the try whose last statement is COMMIT, the layout of retention.py:105-132.
checks.result: Confirmed in 5 of 5 attempts (Python 3.13.16, SQLite 3.45.1, WAL, synchronous=FULL, a 20k-row transaction whose COMMIT took about 0.27 s, timer SIGINT at dur/3). Each time KeyboardInterrupt was raised in the inner except after the commit was durable (20000 rows committed). ROLLBACK then raised 'cannot rollback - no transaction is active' and the outer except ran, which in prune is where the archive is unlinked.

checks.invariant: Prune removes only audit rows before the first row at or after the cutoff and only approvals in denied/executed/failed/expired. Deletions it did not perform are still detected by verify()/verify_archives().
checks.result: Holds. _plan (retention.py:54-64) selects id < MIN(id WHERE ts >= cutoff). Timestamps share the UTC millisecond isoformat used by _cutoff (retention.py:44-51), and the future cutoff is rejected. DELETE is bounded by the planned last id (retention.py:114). Approvals are planned by terminal status; claim moves only pending rows (approvals.py:82-89) and finish runs only after claim (service.py:406-483), so a terminal status cannot revert before the id-only delete. h.py check3: pending and approved rows were kept and 4 terminal rows were pruned. verify and verify_archives were ok after the prune. Deleting the first row after the anchor was detected (id gap at #7). tests/test_retention.py: 7 passed in the sandbox (pytest.out, not promoted). insert_record chains from the latest anchor only when the table is empty (audit.py:228-243), and verify() fails on an anchor with an empty table (audit.py:343-344).

checks.invariant: Concurrent server writes and concurrent prunes cannot make prune delete unarchived rows or leave the append-only trigger missing.
checks.result: Holds. The plan is read outside the lock, but the audit table is append-only, so planned rows cannot change. Inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, prune re-checks MIN(id) against the planned first row and the latest anchor (retention.py:108-111). DROP TRIGGER / DELETE / CREATE TRIGGER from NO_DELETE_SQL (audit.py:56-59) all run in the same write transaction, so other connections (AuditLog.append BEGIN IMMEDIATE, audit.py:294) never see the trigger missing, and ROLLBACK restores it on error. An approvals-only prune reuses the latest anchor, or (0, GENESIS), inside the transaction (retention.py:117), so verify_archives' per-archive last-row check (audit.py:370) stays consistent. The remaining in-DB anchor forgeability is the documented README limit and is not reported.

checks.invariant: If the archive cannot be written, nothing is deleted (README.md:190) and the archive state stays clean.
checks.result: The DB is unchanged, but a partial file is left behind. h.py check2 simulated ENOSPC on the third gzip write: prune raised OSError 28, the DB still held 7 rows and no anchor, a 297-byte partial archive remained, and a re-run with the same path failed with FileExistsError. _write_archive (retention.py:67-84) runs before the try that unlinks. No audit loss, so recorded as hardening.

checks.invariant: Archive serialization and verification match live verify. A sha-pinned archive cannot carry forged audit rows, and parsing it does not amplify beyond operator-supplied content.
checks.result: Holds. _write_archive uses json.dumps (escapes control characters, so TextIOWrapper universal-newline splitting is safe) and read_archive rebuilds the same column tuples (audit.py:208-225). check_chain recomputes hashes from GENESIS across archives into the live table (audit.py:360-378), so content swapped after the sha check (TOCTOU between read_bytes at :362 and read_archive at :364) cannot change the audit rows without breaking the chain. Approval rows in the archive are protected only by that sha check and are not otherwise verified. The archive is operator-supplied and pinned to an anchor sha, and its size is bounded by the pruned DB rows.

candidates.title: Interrupted prune deletes the only archive of audit rows it has already committed as pruned
candidates.description: retention.prune writes the archive, then deletes the audit and approval rows and records an anchor holding the archive's sha256 in one transaction. Its outer error handler unlinks the archive on any BaseException without checking whether that transaction committed. A Ctrl-C (SIGINT) that arrives while the fsync-bound COMMIT runs is raised by CPython right after COMMIT returns, still inside the inner try. The handler's ROLLBACK then fails with 'no transaction is active', and the outer handler deletes the archive. Result: the DB says rows 1..N were pruned into an archive with a recorded sha256, that archive no longer exists, verify() reports the chain intact ('pruned through #N'), and verify_archives can never pass again. The pruned audit history and its tamper evidence are gone for good, which breaks the stated invariant that a failed prune leaves the database and archive consistent.
candidates.root_cause: The cleanup in retention.py:130-131 (`except BaseException: archive.unlink(missing_ok=True)`) is keyed on 'an exception happened' rather than 'the prune transaction did not commit'. The inner handler (retention.py:127-129) runs ROLLBACK unconditionally even when conn.in_transaction is already False after a successful COMMIT (retention.py:126). Any exception that surfaces after COMMIT completes, such as KeyboardInterrupt delivered during COMMIT, therefore destroys the archive that the committed anchor (retention.py:118-121) refers to.
candidates.intended_behavior: The archive is removed only if the prune transaction did not commit. Once the anchor row referencing the archive's sha256 is durable, the archive must be kept whatever exception follows, and the failure must be reported as 'pruned; archive kept at <path>'.

trace.description: Host operator runs `agentbox prune --before ... --archive ...`, which calls retention.prune on Settings().db_path.
The archive is written, fsynced, and its sha256 computed before the transaction.
Inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, audit rows are deleted and an audit_anchor row with the archive name and sha256 is inserted.
COMMIT makes the deletion and anchor durable. A SIGINT pending during this call is raised as KeyboardInterrupt immediately after it returns, still inside the inner try.
Unconditional ROLLBACK raises OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active'), which chains on the KeyboardInterrupt.
archive.unlink deletes the only copy of the rows the committed anchor says were archived.

evidence.description: The archive is unlinked on any BaseException with no check of commit state.
ROLLBACK is issued without checking conn.in_transaction, so it raises after a successful COMMIT.
verify() starts at the latest anchor, so it keeps passing after the archive is lost and hides the loss.
verify_archives needs the archive whose sha256 the anchor holds. With it deleted, full-history verification is impossible from then on.
cmd_prune catches only ValueError/FileExistsError/RuntimeError. The OperationalError surfaces as a traceback, and a re-run reports nothing to prune.

conditions.description: Host operator running the prune CLI with direct DB file access. No remote or agent principal is involved.

SIGINT (Ctrl-C or a supervisor such as `timeout -s INT`) arrives while COMMIT executes, or in the few bytecodes after it inside the inner try. COMMIT of a large prune is fsync-bound (about 0.27 s for 20k 1 KB rows in the sandbox, longer on large production DBs).
At least one audit row is older than the cutoff, so prune reaches the transaction.

execution.attacker_perspective: Operator mistake the code claims to handle (interrupted prune). No adversary is needed. The effect is loss of audit-log integrity evidence for the pruned range.
payloads: h.py check1: AuditLog fixture with 5 rows before the cutoff and 2 after; retention.sqlite3 shimmed to a Connection subclass whose execute('COMMIT') calls the real COMMIT and then signal.raise_signal(SIGINT); prune(db, cut, 'c1.jsonl.gz')

h2.py: WAL DB, synchronous=FULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE + 20000 randomblob(1000) inserts; threading.Timer(dur/3) sends os.kill(getpid(), SIGINT) during a real COMMIT inside the same nested try/except layout as retention.prune
instructions: Run tools/sbx h-retention /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h.py (no network, read-only /target, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 120 s) and read check1 output.
Run tools/sbx h-retention /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h2.py to show that a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real COMMIT surfaces in the inner except after the commit is durable.
execution.observed_result: check1: prune raised OperationalError, context KeyboardInterrupt. Archive exists after failure: False. Audit table now holds rows 6-8 with anchor (seq 1, last_id 5, 'c1.jsonl.gz', sha 3628529612...). verify(): ok=True, pruned_through=5. verify_archives([archive]) raised FileNotFoundError; verify_archives([]) returned ok=False ('anchor count 1, archives 0'). h2: 5/5 attempts gave inner-except KeyboardInterrupt, then ROLLBACK raised 'cannot rollback - no transaction is active', then the outer except ran, with 20000 rows committed.

remediation.strategy: Make archive cleanup depend on the DB's commit state, not on whether an exception was raised. Roll back only while a transaction is active. Before unlinking, check whether the anchor for this archive's sha256 exists, and keep the archive if it does. Also fsync the parent directory after creating the archive so the anchor never outlives its archive's directory entry after a crash. Regression test: a Connection factory that raises KeyboardInterrupt after a successful COMMIT must leave the archive in place, and verify_archives([archive]) must pass.

likelihood.reason: Requires the operator (or a supervisor) to send SIGINT during the COMMIT of a host-only CLI command. The window is short but real for large prunes, which are the intended use (disk pressure), and Ctrl-C on a slow-looking command is a common operator action.

impact.reason: The only remaining copy of the pruned audit rows (and finished approvals) is permanently destroyed, while the in-DB anchor and verify() report the history as cleanly archived. Tamper evidence for the whole pruned range becomes unverifiable from then on. No confidentiality impact and no remote attacker.

confidence.reason: Source path is direct. The end-to-end prune harness reproduced archive deletion after commit, and a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real COMMIT surfaced in the inner except in 5 of 5 runs on CPython 3.13.

hardening: retention._write_archive (retention.py:67-84) runs before the try that unlinks on failure, so ENOSPC or another write error leaves a partial archive. It wastes disk during the exact low-disk scenario prune exists for and blocks a re-run with FileExistsError (h.out check2). Wrap the write and unlink on failure.

The archive sha256 is computed by re-reading the path after close (retention.py:84), and verify_archives hashes the file (audit.py:362) and then re-opens it to parse (audit.py:364). Hash the bytes as written and parse the same buffer that was hashed. Archived approval rows are protected only by this sha check.
The parent directory is not fsynced after creating the archive, so a power loss after COMMIT could keep the anchor but lose the archive's directory entry. Add os.fsync on the directory fd.

The archive is created with the default umask (open 'xb', retention.py:70) and carries full finished approval rows, including the unmasked result column and any args left raw when _finish failed. Create it 0600, since README tells operators to store it elsewhere.

AuditLog.verify (audit.py:338-340) and verify_archives (audit.py:354-357) read the anchor and rows as separate autocommit statements. A prune committing between them gives a false 'id gap' alarm. This fails closed; wrapping both reads in one read transaction removes the false positive.

Capture PNGs are indexed only through approval rows (service.py:114-116 drop_captures). An orphan capture from the create-then-write window (service.py:337-341) or a failed unlink is no longer reachable by sandbox-delete cleanup once prune removes its approval row. Prune could also unlink captures/<aid>.png for pruned approvals.
